The plan in one screen

Three things shape every route

Bangladeshi MBBS (2019–20 session), results out September 2026, internship from Oct–Nov 2026 in Chattogram, no work experience, USD 30k budget. Long-term goal: practise medicine in the US. Fields: public health, epidemiology, global health, clinical research, aerospace medicine.

  1. 1

    Finish the internship

    Without it there is no full BMDC registration, so no FCPS, full GMC, Saudi, Qatar or UAE licence, and no AHPRA registration. Realistic time to leave: December 2027 to April 2028.

  2. 2

    Best bridge to the US

    Take Step 1 during the internship, then a paid US research job, then Step 2 CK, aiming for the 2029 Match. That keeps the graduation recent (about 3 years) and earns US letters of recommendation.

  3. 3

    Apply now, start later

    Erasmus Mundus, Gates Cambridge, KAUST, MEXT, GKS, Stipendium Hungaricum, Türkiye and CSC need no work experience. Most 2027 starts collide with the internship, so ask each programme about late arrival or aim for 2028.

Timeline from now to the 2029 Match

  1. Nov 2026 – Jan 2027 Now

    The application wave

    Funded master's and PhD deadlines cluster here. One master motivation letter, adapted per programme.

  2. Nov 2026 – late 2027

    Internship year

    Unlocks full BMDC registration — the key to every licence route.

  3. 2027

    USMLE Step 1

    Sit it during the internship. Decide on PLAB 1 before Dhaka sittings end in Feb 2027.

  4. Dec 2027 – Apr 2028

    Departure window

    Internship done. Start a funded degree, or a paid research post abroad.

  5. 2028

    US research job + Step 2 CK

    J-1 Research Scholar or H-1B cap-exempt post. US letters. ECFMG Pathway + OET.

  6. March 2029 Goal

    The Match

    Graduation still recent, US experience in hand.

    Paid US research post (J-1 or H-1B cap-exempt)

    Opens after internship

    Rolling; start emailing PIs May–Jul 2027

    Full notes & source

    The fastest real exit and the best bridge to a US Match: US letters and recent graduation. Avoid unpaid posts. Visa: J-1 research scholar is safest (ECFMG can sponsor if the host can't). H-1B $100k fee: Proclamation 11069 (18 Sep 2026) extends it to 21 Sep 2027, but a California court vacated the agency policies applying it on 30 Sep (government appealed to the 9th Circuit, 9 Oct) and a Massachusetts ruling also blocks it; appeals pending in the 1st, 9th and D.C. Circuits; as of 15 Oct no court had stayed the rulings (law-firm summaries; dockets not verified). The DHS $103,265 proposal's comment period closed 24 Sep with no final rule. DHS proposed (25 Aug 2026) an extra $103,265 fee for cap-subject petitions only — cap-exempt university employers wouldn't pay it. J-1 'duration of status' rule postponed by a court on 14 Sep. Keep his online presence clean before a J-1 interview. 1 Nov: no new court ruling found; university ISSS guidance (7 Oct) still says the fee is not being collected.

  • USA · Clinical licensing

    USMLE + ECFMG certification

    Open to him now

    2027 Pathways close 31 Jan 2027; 2028 Pathways not announced

    Money
    USD 695 + 210 surcharge (Step 1), 695 + 235 (Step 2 CK), $945 Pathway + OET
    Timing
    Step 1 in 2027, Match 2029
    Gets him
    Leads to practising medicine
    US goal
    Helps the US goal
    Full notes & source

    Step 1 and Step 2 CK plus a Pathway (OET Medicine) are required; with no licence, Pathway 6 (Mini-CEX) is the realistic one. IMGs now apply for USMLE via FSMB (since 12 Jan 2026). Step 2 CK is the score screen. Check the school's ECFMG Sponsor Note on wdoms.org. NRMP 2027 Match: registration opened 15 Sep 2026 (multi-factor login now mandatory), registration deadline 29 Jan 2027, ECFMG requirements due by the rank-list deadline 3 Mar 2027, Match Day 19 Mar 2027 — too early for him; target 2028 or 2029. Policy: the 75-country immigrant-visa pause (Bangladesh included) is no longer in effect since 21 Aug 2026 (court order in CLINIC v. Rubio) — good news for a later green card, but litigation continues. The DHS rule ending J-1 'duration of status' (due 15 Sep 2026) was postponed by a court; ECFMG is watching. As of 1 Nov the only recent ECFMG news post is still the D/S postponement (23 Sep); no 2028 Pathways, OET or fee news. NRMP published three new transition-to-residency data reports on 14 Oct (no rule change). USMLE now uses new software with 30-minute blocks (Step 1: 14 × 30 min since 14 May 2026; Step 2 CK: 16 × 30 min since 7 May 2026) — practise with the new tutorial. Bangladesh is not on the US travel-ban list. NRMP's Oct 2026 Illuminator: programs must give applicants at least 48 hours to answer interview invitations and can't over-invite; a voluntary rank-list lock pilot runs in IM, Pediatrics and Vascular Surgery — no IMG-specific rule change.

    Official source for USMLE + ECFMG certification (opens in a new tab) ↗Verified 1 Nov 2026

    Medical Training (Prioritisation) Act: regulations laid 15 Sep 2026 for training posts starting in 2027 give priority at both shortlisting and offer to UK, Irish and EEA-EFTA graduates, doctors who completed UK Foundation or the prior training stage, and British citizens / ILR / settled status holders. A fresh IMG on a visa is not prioritised, so PLAB now leads mainly to non-training (trust-grade) jobs first. Registration must be applied for within 2 years of passing PLAB 2. 2026/27 fee page not re-verified. Immigration rules HC 584 (stages 8 Oct, 29 Oct, 30 Nov, 9 Dec 2026) amend Skilled Worker — details not verified; Graduate route drops to 18 months from 1 Jan 2027. Ireland's Medical Council now accepts a PLAB 2 pass in place of PRES (confirmed 24 Oct), so PLAB also opens Ireland. HC 584 Skilled Worker changes from 8 Oct are mainly about modern-slavery victims and sponsor rules — nothing doctor-specific found. GMC (gmc-uk.org news, announced May 2026): PLAB 1 will no longer be held in Dhaka from February 2027 (also Alexandria, Accra, Chennai); overseas sittings drop from four to three a year. After that he must sit PLAB 1 in another country (e.g. one of the remaining Indian centres) or in the UK — extra visa and travel cost.

How to read it. 0 means no funded route exists. 1–2 is a long shot: elite schemes with a few dozen awards, usually won by people with research records. 3 is an outside chance worth a strong application. Open any route for the four-factor breakdown and what would raise the score.

The pattern. Nothing scores above 4 right now. The best odds are the government schemes where Bangladesh is a partner (Stipendium Hungaricum, CSC) and the health-focused Erasmus Mundus programmes. The biggest levers are the same everywhere: a class-rank certificate, one research output during the internship, and applying to intakes you can actually start (January 2028 or later).

Unanswered

Open questions that decide several routes

Each one is worth an email. The answer can open or close several routes at once.

  1. When is the MBBS conferred?

    Before or only after the internship? It decides SpaceMed, Commonwealth Shared, Maastricht and others that need the degree finished by a deadline.

  2. Maastricht admission route

    Bachelor's route (GRE needed) or bachelor's + master's route (no GRE)? Does his average convert to at least 7.5/10? Ask masteradmission-fhml@maastrichtuniversity.nl.

  3. Swedish Institute's 3,000 hours

    Paid or freelance work separate from the internship, before Feb 2027. The SI FAQ says internships don't count.

  4. Hopkins work-experience line

    The one-year line appears on the ScM page, not the PhD page. Ask BSPH.EpiAcademic@jh.edu whether the internship counts.

  5. MBBS → direct PhD in Australia and NZ

    No university says an MBBS alone qualifies. It's case by case (publications, research), with an MPhil as fallback.

  6. WES timing

    Starting in early November lands mid-December — too late for a verified 1 Dec file. Ask Hopkins and Emory if WES can follow.

Today's deadline: only if a supervisor has said yes

The Imperial College President's PhD Scholarships are the most prestigious doctoral funding Imperial offers. They're fully funded and a real route into world-class research, but the first round closes at 23:59 UK time today, and without a supervisor's agreement you're not ready for it.

✦ Drafted by Gemini (an AI), then rewritten and fact-checked against official pages on 2 Nov 2026. Where they disagreed, the official page won.

  • Poor fitUS Match, 2029 planA 3.5-year PhD pushes a US Match out to about 2031–32.

  • Good fitYour interestsPublic health, epidemiology and global health departments all sit here.

Before you board

PortalImperial online application (via the scheme page) ↗ (opens in a new tab)

Imperial states there is no application fee for PhDs (taught master's cost £90). No separate scholarship form: apply for the PhD place and select the President's PhD Scholarship in the funding section; the department then nominates you.

How this was checked: Fee quote from Imperial's postgraduate admissions page (Muse, 2 Nov). The scheme page rendered blank for a live re-read, so dates and stipend come from the board's weekly sweep.

01

What it pays

  • Full tuition fees at the overseas rate.
  • £27,036 a year tax-free stipend for up to 3.5 years, plus £2,000 a year for research costs.
  • About 50 awards a year, open to any nationality.
  • Your $30,000 budget stays untouched: it can go to USMLE fees and US clinical experience instead.

02

Who can apply

  • Any nationality, Bangladesh included.
  • A first-class degree or equivalent. How Imperial reads an MBBS comes down to your marks and class rank.
  • A supervisor's agreement first: find a faculty member in an area like the School of Public Health, email them your CV and a short proposal, and get their yes before you apply.

03

Dates that matter

  • Round 1: 2 Nov 2026 (decisions by 31 Jan 2027).
  • Round 2: 11 Jan 2027. Round 3: 1 Mar 2027.
  • Funded 2027–28 places can start as late as 1 Nov 2027, which brushes against the end of your internship.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

A PhD from Imperial in public health makes you exceptionally competitive for academic residency programmes, and London gives you a base for PLAB and NHS contacts. But the plan that works for 2029 is Step 1 during the internship, a paid US research job, then Step 2 CK. A 3.5-year PhD replaces that plan rather than adding to it, and your Match year moves to roughly 2031–32.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: timing

    Round 1 closes today. If you have no agreed supervisor, aim for round 2 on 11 Jan instead.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: competition

    Fifty awards across the whole college, usually for people with research experience. A fresh MBBS with no publications needs a strong supervisor connection.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: years since graduation

    Many US programmes screen on how long ago you graduated. A PhD explains the gap well for academic programmes, less so for community ones.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: clinical distance

    Three and a half years in a research group means arranging observerships before you reapply to residency.

06

The honest recommendation

Treat this as a physician-scientist route, not a 2029 route. Apply in round 2 if a supervisor commits in the next two months. Otherwise keep your energy on Step 1 and a paid US research post.

Brilliant funding, wrong field for epidemiology

OIST is an elite, English-language graduate university on Okinawa with one of the most generous PhD packages anywhere. It's basic science and computation rather than public health, so the question is whether you'd want a lab life for five years.

Before you board

PortalOIST graduate school application ↗ (opens in a new tab)

Non-refundable, and OIST offers no waivers for personal financial situations. Check a supervisor has room for students before you apply.

How this was checked: Confirmed live on oist.jp/admissions/phd-program/apply-phd (2 Nov 2026).

01

What it is

A single 5-year integrated PhD. The first two years are lab rotations and coursework, and the last three are thesis research. There are no departments: units cover molecular and cell biology, neuroscience, mathematics and computation, chemistry, physics and ecology.

02

What it pays

  • Tuition included, with a stipend of about ¥2.6 million a year, rising to about ¥3.6 million.
  • Support for relocation and conference travel.
  • Cost to apply: ¥5,000, non-refundable and without waivers. It's small, but it isn't free.

03

Who can apply

  • Completion of a bachelor's, master's or equivalent before the admission date. Medicine isn't named, so confirm with admissions that an MBBS is accepted.
  • Check that your chosen unit actually has room to supervise new PhD students. OIST warns that strong applicants are rejected when the field has no space.

04

Dates that matter

  • 15 Nov 2026, 23:59 JST for the 2027 admissions workshop round.
  • Entry on 1 May or 1 Sep 2027, or 1 Jan 2028. The January 2028 entry is the one that fits the end of your internship.

05

How it fits the US and Europe goals

A PhD with strong papers helps for academic residencies, but US programmes weigh clinical experience and clinical research more heavily than bench work. Europe's licensing routes (PLAB, the German Kenntnisprüfung, Ireland's PRES) don't change at all.

06

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: timeline

    Starting in 2028 and finishing five years later puts a US Match at roughly 2033.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: field mismatch

    There is no public health or epidemiology unit. Computational biology is your closest door.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: admission

    Research experience matters a lot, and you'd be competing with people who have lab degrees.

07

The honest recommendation

Apply only if you're deliberately choosing a research career and would lean into computational work. For a Match-focused plan, skip it.

Exceptional if you can show genomics and coding skills

The Wellcome Sanger Institute 4-year PhD is one of the best-funded doctorates in the world, with a Cambridge degree at the end. It's a genomics and data-science programme, so it only works if that's the work you want.

✦ Drafted by Gemini (an AI), then rewritten and fact-checked against official pages on 2 Nov 2026. Where they disagreed, the official page won.

  • Poor fitUS Match, 2029 planFour years pushes a Match to about 2032.
  • MixedPractising in EuropeStrong UK academic standing; no licensing shortcut.

What would raise it

  • A genomic-epidemiology question in your statement

Before you board

PortalSanger Institute online application ↗ (opens in a new tab)

Applying to the Sanger costs nothing. If you're selected you then apply to the University of Cambridge, which costs £20 (Cambridge Applicant Portal: apply.postgraduate.study.cam.ac.uk).

How this was checked: Both fee lines confirmed on Sanger's FAQ and Cambridge's fee page (2 Nov 2026).

01

What it is

A 1+3 model. In year one you do three short rotations in different labs plus taught modules, then choose your main project. The degree is awarded by the University of Cambridge, and you work on the Wellcome Genome Campus.

02

What it pays

  • Full university tuition fees and a stipend (£25,270 in year one at Oct 2025 rates).
  • Visa and NHS surcharge costs reimbursed.
  • At least 12 funded studentships, whatever your nationality.
  • Cost to apply: nothing for the Sanger application. If selected, the Cambridge admission application costs £20.

03

Who can apply

  • Candidates expected to hold a 1st or good 2:1, or an equivalent overseas qualification. Whether your MBBS is read that way is worth asking.
  • Genomics and data science are the focus. Basic Python or R and some statistics will help an MBBS profile a lot.

04

Dates that matter

  • 24 Nov 2026, 09:00 GMT is the closing time.
  • Start is in October 2027, which is likely to collide with your internship: ask whether a later start is possible before spending time on the application.

05

How it fits the US and Europe goals

A Cambridge-linked PhD with strong genomics papers is a great physician-scientist credential and can put you in contact with US collaborators for letters. It doesn't give you US clinical experience, and a four-year PhD moves a Match to around 2032.

06

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: scope

    This is genomics and computation, not general public health.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: preparation

    Selection favours people with coding or lab skills you may not have built yet.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: clinical distance

    Four years away from patients means rebuilding clinical credibility afterwards.

07

The honest recommendation

If genomic epidemiology really pulls you, ask Sanger about starting later and whether an MBBS qualifies, and spend the internship building Python and R skills. If the 2029 Match is the priority, this isn't the route.

01

What it pays

  • CHF 13,500 per semester living allowance plus a tuition waiver.
  • About 60 awards, based on merit rather than financial need.
  • Cost to apply: CHF 150 per programme (non-Swiss degree), non-refundable, no waivers. There's no extra ESOP fee.

02

Who can apply

  • Strong results in your degree, roughly the top 10% of your class.
  • A Master's application to ETH for the autumn semester, with a thesis pre-proposal you write yourself. That pre-proposal carries a lot of weight.
  • Typical English requirement is around IELTS 7.0 or TOEFL 100; check your programme's page.

03

Dates that matter

  • The window is 1–30 Nov 2026, with a September 2027 start. That start collides with the internship, so ask about a later one or plan for the next cycle.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

An ETH MSc in health sciences, statistics or biomedical engineering looks excellent on a residency application, and it links to aerospace physiology research. What it can't do is give you US clinical experience or any shortcut to practise in Switzerland or the EU, where you'd still need the local recognition exams and the language.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: competition

    You need rank and a strong research idea, not just good marks.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: course fit

    ETH's health degrees are quantitative and molecular; there's no standard MPH.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: timeline

    One and a half to two years away from the USMLE track pushes a Match to about 2031.

06

The honest recommendation

Apply only if you want a quantitative research career and can write a convincing thesis pre-proposal. For a clinical Match, skip it. For European practice, Germany's Kenntnisprüfung or the UK's PLAB are more direct.

01

What it pays

  • Full course fees plus a living grant for the whole degree.
  • A MSc in Global Health Science & Epidemiology carries overseas fees of about £36,900 (2027–28), so funding it yourself isn't realistic.
  • Cost to apply: £75 for taught courses or £20 for research courses. Applicants resident in a listed low-income country, Bangladesh included, can have it waived.

02

Who can apply

  • Any nationality, any subject. Medicine degrees are accepted.
  • The course deadline is what counts: everyone who applies by it and gets an offer is considered.
  • Skip the MSc in International Health and Tropical Medicine: it asks for 3+ years of low-resource work experience, which you don't have yet.

03

  • 1 Dec 2026, 12:00 UK for the MSc in Global Health Science & Epidemiology. The Oxford and NDPH pages served older-cycle text on re-check, so confirm on the Graduate Admissions page.
  • An October 2027 start collides with the internship. The next realistic cycle is December 2027 for October 2028.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

A one-year Oxford MSc in epidemiology is the strongest version of an academic credential you can get quickly, and Oxford's population-health groups have US collaborations that can lead to letters. It's still not US clinical experience, and in the UK it doesn't replace PLAB.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: competition

    You can't apply to Clarendon directly. You need a place first, and marks and rank near the top.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: timing

    The cycle that fits your internship is next year's.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: exam clash

    An Oxford MSc plus Step 2 CK preparation in the same year is a heavy load.

06

The honest recommendation

Apply for the MSc in Global Health Science & Epidemiology only if you can get a later start or are happy to wait for the 2028 intake. Use the waiver, and never pay course fees from your $30,000.
